prompt: Hand-inked graphic novel character head study, clean confident ink outlines, flat cel shading in a muted sun-faded palette, plain cream paper background, no text. Two views side by side of the same head and shoulders: front view and side profile facing right. An original 15-year-old caboclo boy from a fishing village on the coast of Ceará, Brazil, 1932, of strong Indigenous heritage mixed with African and Portuguese: a broad face with high, prominent cheekbones, dark almond-shaped eyes that are narrower rather than big and round, thick straight dark eyebrows, a broad nose, full lips, a firm jaw. Thick, straight, coarse black hair, cut short and uneven, no waves and no gray or light highlights. Warm bronze-brown skin deeply tanned by sun and sea, no rosy cheeks. A grounded, serious-but-warm look, a real teenager, not a child; an original character, not a caricature. He wears an open collar of a faded reddish-brown homespun cotton shirt. No hat.
